subtopic: Money attitudes, family finances, gifting, borrowing between relatives
passage: I'm Tanuja, and I live next door to Farhan's family. On Eid, Farhan's Nani pressed a crisp note into his palm and everyone smiled. Farhan, nearly two, waved it like a flag. At the corner shop his father put coins into the shopkeeper's hand and Farhan got a toffee. He clapped. Then he pressed a coin into my hand, beaming. I cannot know what he was thinking. Perhaps he has noticed that handing things over makes grown-ups smile.

qa.q: What did Farhan's Nani press into his palm on Eid?
qa.a: She pressed a crisp note into his palm.

qa.q: What might Farhan have felt when he pressed a coin into Tanuja's hand?
qa.a: He seemed delighted, since he was beaming, though the narrator says the exact thought cannot be known.

qa.q: How could an adult respond to Farhan's giving and waving of the note?
qa.a: An adult could smile and say thank you when he hands something over, and keep the note safe, so the giving stays a happy game.

qa.q: What does Tanuja think Farhan has noticed about the grown-ups?
qa.a: Tanuja thinks Farhan has noticed that handing things over makes the grown-ups smile.

grounding: A toddler sees notes given as blessings and coins bought sweets, and understands only that giving pleases people.

Monday: Dada pressed a shiny coin into Wasim's fist. Wasim, twenty months old, tapped it on the floor and carried it everywhere.
Wednesday: At the corner shop his mother Pooja put the coin in the shopkeeper's hand, and Wasim got a sweet. He laughed.
Saturday: Wasim found the coin under the sofa, held it out to Pooja, and opened his other hand.

qa.q: Who gave Wasim the shiny coin?
qa.a: Dada gave Wasim the shiny coin.

qa.q: What did Wasim seem to be feeling when the shopkeeper handed him a sweet?
qa.a: He felt happy and delighted, shown by how he laughed.

qa.q: How could Pooja respond when Wasim holds out the coin and his open hand?
qa.a: Pooja could smile, take the coin, and give him a sweet, so the exchange stays a happy game.

qa.q: What might Pooja see in Wasim's handing over the coin on Saturday?
qa.a: Pooja may see that Wasim has learned that the coin turns into a sweet, and that giving the coin to her pleases her.

grounding: A toddler sees coins handed over for sweets and learns only that giving pleases people.

passage:
At the Diwali gathering, Vaibhav, two, watched Dada press a crisp note into cousin Saurabh's hand. Everyone clapped and smiled. Saurabh touched Dada's feet.
Vaibhav toddled to Dada holding his soggy biscuit and pushed it into Dada's palm. Then he bent and patted Dada's feet.
Everyone laughed. Dada laughed loudest and kissed his head. Vaibhav clapped for himself.

qa.q: What did Dada press into Saurabh's hand?
qa.a: Dada pressed a crisp note into cousin Saurabh's hand.

qa.q: What was Vaibhav probably feeling when he clapped for himself?
qa.a: Vaibhav probably felt happy and proud, enjoying the laughter and smiles that giving brought.

qa.q: What could adults gently show Vaibhav about giving?
qa.a: They could keep praising his giving and smiles, since at his age he understands only that giving pleases people.

qa.q: How might Dada feel when Vaibhav gives him the biscuit?
qa.a: Dada seems delighted and touched, laughing loudest and kissing his head.

grounding: A toddler watches money given as a blessing and copies the giving with a biscuit, understanding only that giving makes people smile.

subtopic: Money attitudes, family finances, gifting, borrowing between relatives
passage:
"Rukmini, look! Nani gave me money!" Disha waved a note.
"Mine!" Rukmini, two, reached for it.
"No, it's for my birthday."
Nani laughed. "Here, Rukmini." She gave her a shiny coin.
Rukmini stared at it. She bit it.
"Not in the mouth!" Mumma said.
Rukmini held the coin up to the light and giggled. Then she gave it back to Nani.
"For you!"
Nani laughed and hugged her. Rukmini beamed.

qa.q: What did Nani give Rukmini?
qa.a: Nani gave her a shiny coin.

qa.q: Why did Rukmini giggle at the coin?
qa.a: She felt delighted by the shiny object and happy with the attention.

qa.q: What might help Rukmini as she learns about money?
qa.a: Letting her enjoy giving and receiving with smiles, and keeping coins away from her mouth, suits her age.

qa.q: How does Nani seem to feel when Rukmini gives the coin back?
qa.a: Nani seems amused and warmed, laughing and hugging her.

grounding: A toddler sees money given as a blessing, treats a coin as a shiny object and gives it back, learning only that giving brings smiles.

passage:
Daycare note, Tuesday.
During free play, Swati, two, set up a "shop" with leaves. She handed a leaf to Amandeep and said, "Paisa!" Amandeep gave her a block. Both clapped.
Swati handed out leaves to everyone, smiling each time someone said "thank you." She did not want anything back.
She understands giving makes people happy.
Next step: we'll add a toy till to the play corner.

qa.q: What did Swati use as money in her shop?
qa.a: She used leaves.

qa.q: How did Swati seem to feel when people said "thank you"?
qa.a: Swati seemed happy and pleased, smiling each time.

qa.q: Why is a toy till a good next step?
qa.a: It builds on Swati's play in a fun way, since at her age money is just a shiny, happy exchange.

qa.q: How might Amandeep have felt during the game?
qa.a: Amandeep probably enjoyed it too, clapping after trading a block for a leaf.

grounding: A daycare note shows a toddler copying money exchanges in play, understanding only that giving pleases people.

passage: At the wedding in the village, Dadaji pressed a folded note into the bride's hand. Everyone smiled and clapped. Gargi, just two, watched from Maa's lap. Later her cousin Tushar gave her a shiny coin. Gargi held it up, then toddled over and pushed it into Dadaji's palm. Dadaji laughed and kissed her head. Gargi clapped, just like the grown-ups, and held out her hand for the coin again.

qa.q: What did Tushar give Gargi?
qa.a: Tushar gave her a shiny coin.

qa.q: Why did Gargi push the coin into Dadaji's palm?
qa.a: Gargi seemed delighted by the smiles and wanted to join in, copying the giving that made everyone happy.

qa.q: How could the family gently build on this moment?
qa.a: They can smile and say thank you when she gives, and let her play at giving and taking, since at this age the joy of sharing matters more than money.

qa.q: What might it be like for Dadaji when Gargi gives him the coin?
qa.a: Dadaji is amused and touched, laughing and kissing her head at the little copy of his blessing.

grounding: It illustrates a toddler who watches money given as blessings and understands only that giving makes adults smile.
